claims.text: Combining finite-temperature ab initio calculations with machine-learning corrections can improve electronic-conductivity predictions for oxygen-containing HfNbTaTiZr relative to perfect-crystal analytical models.
The modeled bulk HfNbTaTiZr contains approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
Oxygen is randomly incorporated as point defects in the HfNbTaTiZr specimen.
A predictive framework can combine finite-temperature ab initio calculations with machine-learning calibration using experimental data.
The 0–200 K conductivity regime is dominated by reduced phonon scattering and possible quantum effects.
Enhanced phonon interactions are significant in the 300–1200 K regime.
Defect migration is significant in the 300–1200 K regime.
Oxygen-induced defect states alter the local electronic structure of HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen-induced defect states alter phonon-scattering pathways in HfNbTaTiZr.
Interstitial oxygen changes electronic scattering mechanisms and vibrational disorder.
Machine-learning calibration can capture defect-related deviations from ideal-crystal conductivity behavior.
The defect-inclusive model will reduce conductivity-prediction error by roughly 10% or more relative to conventional analytical predictions in both specified temperature regimes.
Conventional conductivity models for this alloy assume perfect, defect-free crystals and neglect oxygen-induced scattering.
Conventional analytical conductivity predictions differ from measurements by more than 20%.
The proposed model is expected to be reliable over 0–200 K and 300–1200 K for bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing oxygen near 1 wt.%.
Predictions outside the stated temperature ranges or at substantially different oxygen concentrations may be less accurate.
Prediction improvement depends on the nature and spatial distribution of oxygen defects and on coupling effects omitted from preliminary ab initio approximations.
